subject: Narrowing ancillary-loss exclusion — MSA + Order Form alignment
messages:
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acerohealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Revised MSA redline — consequential/ancillary loss language

Rachel — thanks for the call earlier. Per our legal team's review we've attached a marked MSA and a short note on the Order Form. The main outstanding item for us is the breadth of the 'excluded losses' carve-out. The current draft reads broad and Acero is asking for: (1) explicit examples of "ancillary/knock-on" losses that are excluded, and (2) confirmation that punitive damages remain excluded but incidental recovery for certain regulatory fines be preserved.

High level ask: keep exclusion mutual where possible but carve back for (a) claims that are direct and arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, and (b) third-party regulatory fines that are not punitive in nature.

See attached MSA_Acero_v2_redline.docx and OrderForm_Acero_markup.pdf for inline suggested edits. Can you confirm whether Redwood is open to a short 'exceptions list' instead of a large definition sweep? We prefer clarity in the Order Form (so customer teams can reason about risk) rather than a one-size exclusion.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Turner
Head of Procurement, Acero Health
Emily Turner | Acero Health

Attachments: MSA_Acero_v2_redline.docx (docx), OrderForm_Acero_markup.pdf (pdf)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acerohealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Revised MSA redline — consequential/ancillary loss language

Emily — appreciate the quick turn. Looping in Legal (karthik) and Contracts (Laura) to get a concise path forward.

Short answer: we want to keep the exclusion mutual and narrow the list of carve-backs to protect our units from open‑ended downstream claims, but we also recognize the customer's need for clarity. Two potential approaches from our side:

1) "Illustrative examples" approach: keep a short set of non-exhaustive examples in the Order Form (e.g., "loss of profits, loss of business, consequential downstream data loss") and retain a mutual exclusion for incidental/special/punitive, with an exceptions paragraph for willful misconduct and direct damages.

2) "Defined threshold" approach: retain a mutual exclusion but allow recovery for third-party regulatory fines or direct statutory penalties where we have materially contributed and the claim is not punitive (subject to caps).

Our preference is option 1 for speed — illustrated examples help both legal and procurement teams operationalize the Order Form. That said, if you need the threshold approach for Acero's audit/compliance, we can draft narrow language.

Karthik — can you propose wording that (a) preserves a mutual exclusion, (b) lists 3–4 short illustrative items in the Order Form, and (c) explicitly states that punitive damages (as defined under governing law) remain excluded except for willful misconduct?

If that's acceptable to you, we'll send a single tracked-change file back for sign-off and have Laura handle commercial acceptance.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-19 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Revised MSA redline — consequential/ancillary loss language

Thanks Rachel — drafting below; feedback welcome. I tried to balance Acero's ask for clarity with Redwood's need to avoid an open-ended exposure.

Proposed bridge language (clean):
"Excluded Losses: Neither party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive or consequential damages, including, without limitation, lost profits, loss of business, loss of data, or loss of use. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the foregoing exclusion shall not apply to (a) damages arising from a party's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud; (b) amounts payable for third‑party claims to the extent such amounts are actually paid by the liable party; and (c) statutory regulatory fines or penalties to the extent recovery for such fines is permitted by applicable law and is expressly listed in the Order Form for the applicable Service."

Notes on intent and risk:
- The clause keeps the exclusion mutual (protects Redwood against asymmetric buyers).
- The parenthetical (c) allows us to agree to carve-in specific regulatory penalties, but only if listed in the Order Form. This provides the visibility Acero wants without creating open liability.
- We should add a sentence in the Order Form that lists the limited non-excluded items (e.g., "Regulatory penalties for failure to comply with HIPAA obligations where Redwood's gross negligence is shown").

Commercial ask: Laura, if we accept (c) we should also confirm whether Acero expects these recoveries to be outside of the monetary cap or included within it. My preference: include within the existing cap to avoid uncapped exposure.

If agreed, Rachel — I'll prepare a tracked-change MSA clean and a one‑page summary bullet list for Acero to sign off.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Rachel / team — thanks for the thoughtful language, that bridge looks promising. Acero is comfortable with mutual exclusion and appreciates the Order Form exception approach (c). Two quick asks before I route internally: (1) can you make explicit that the listed regulatory fines in the Order Form are subject to the overall liability cap (we prefer included, not uncapped), and (2) please add a single sentence clarifying that punitive damages as defined under controlling law remain excluded in all circumstances (we just want the contract to call that out).

If you can send a tracked version with Karthik's bridge edits plus the two tweaks above, I will fast-track through Acero's counsel. Once we have that, we'll finalize commercial redlines and prepare a DocuSign packet.

Best — Emily
